title: Groupoïdes de Teichmüller et les S0 Tg,!ν, S0 TG : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (previous page). A central extension 1 → Π → 𝓔 → μ → 1 is given. A '(Π,μ)-fibration (stricte)' subordinate to it is a groupoid morphism f : C' → C together with: (1) an internal operation of Π on C', i.e. a homomorphism Π → Aut(id_{C'}), so Π acts centrally on every automorphism group; and (2) an external operation of μ on C' by functors, compatible with the Π-operation. Condition (a), also on the previous page, says f is a strict Π-fibration.

This page adds three conditions:
(b) f is μ-equivariant when μ acts trivially on C.
(c) μ acts freely on Ob C' and Ob C'/μ → Ob C is bijective. Hence f is surjective on objects.
(d) The fibres C'_y (y ∈ Ob C) are 'Π-connected' Π-groupoids with operator group μ. Their structure is to be analysed.

Local analysis. Let Φ be a Π-connected Π-groupoid: every Hom_Φ(x,y) is a Π-torsor H_{x,y}, so Φ ≃ BΠ and Π is necessarily abelian. Let μ act strictly on Φ, compatibly with Π, so that E = Ob Φ is a μ-torsor.
- Each α ∈ μ gives isomorphisms α_* : H_{x,y} ≅ H_{αx,αy}.
- The pairs (x,y) with fixed 'difference' u = y^{-1}x ∈ μ form one free transitive μ-orbit. So the α_* form a transitive system of isomorphisms, and all these H_{x,y} can be identified with a single Π-torsor H_u.
- Composition in Φ becomes canonical isomorphisms of Π-torsors H_u ∧^Π H_v ≅ H_{uv} (contracted product), satisfying associativity.

The next page completes the argument. 𝓔_Φ := ⊔_u H_u is a group extension 1 → Π → 𝓔_Φ → μ → 1. Conversely, an extension 𝓔 gives Φ = 𝓔(𝓔), the action groupoid of 𝓔 acting on μ through 𝓔 → μ, with μ acting by transport of structure. Together these give the equivalence (17):
{connected Π-groupoids with a strict compatible μ-action that is free and transitive on objects} ≃ {extensions of μ by Π}.
This is used to define an 𝓔(Π,μ)-structure on C' over C: each fibre C'_y is required to carry a Φ-structure modelled on the fixed extension. It is a local classification step in building central extensions of (Teichmüller) groupoids from fibrations of groupoids.
errors: The notation u = y^{-1}x ∈ μ needs care when μ is non-commutative. For an abstract left μ-torsor E, the element g with x = g·y is conjugated under α (αx = αgα^{-1}·αy). It is therefore not invariant under the diagonal action; the true invariant lives in the inner form Aut_μ(E), which is isomorphic to μ only non-canonically. The argument is correct if E is trivialized (μ acting on itself by left translation, where (αy)^{-1}(αx) = y^{-1}x). The next page's remark that commutativity of μ was not used is therefore true only modulo this choice.
The order of composition (H_u ∧ H_v → H_{uv} versus H_{vu}) depends on conventions and is not specified. This is harmless.

The transitive-system argument needs the μ-action on Φ to be strict, i.e. a genuine homomorphism μ → Aut(Φ) and not a pseudo-action. Grothendieck flags this with 'stricte', but it is essential and implicit in condition (d).
Π-connected with Hom-sets that are Π-torsors forces Aut(x) ≅ Π. Since Π maps to Aut(id), Π must be abelian. The page does not state this explicitly.

ideas.what: Definition of a (Π,μ)-fibration of groupoids subordinate to a central extension: internal central Π-action, external free μ-action on objects, equivariance, Ob C'/μ ≅ Ob C
ideas.modern_name: Groupoid-level model of a central extension / a μ-equivariant Π-banded fibration (related to lifting group actions to gerbes)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Giraud (non-abelian cohomology, 1971) for gerbe language; in Teichmüller-tower context, unsure
ideas.where_published: Not in this form; Esquisse d'un programme discusses Teichmüller groupoids and central extensions only informally

ideas.what: From a Π-connected Π-groupoid with strict μ-action, free and transitive on objects, extract Π-torsors H_u (u ∈ μ) with associative products H_u ∧ H_v ≅ H_{uv}, i.e. a group extension of μ by Π
ideas.modern_name: Extensions as action groupoids / Schreier theory via torsors; a group extension as a 'μ-graded Π-torsor system' (Breen-style)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Schreier; Grothendieck/Giraud (extensions via torsors, SGA7 Exp. VII); Breen
ideas.where_published: SGA 7 I, Exp. VII (biextensions, extensions described via torsors and contracted products); Giraud, Cohomologie non abélienne

ideas.what: Equivalence (17): such μ-equivariant Π-groupoids ↔ extensions of μ by Π
ideas.modern_name: Equivalence between extensions and free transitive equivariant structures on BΠ (action groupoid μ//𝓔)
ideas.where_published: Closest: SGA 7 Exp. VII; Pursuing Stacks has related groupoid material

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a careful but standard local analysis: group extensions are recovered from equivariant torsor-groupoids, which is classical Schreier/Giraud theory phrased in Grothendieck's torsor style. Its only interest is as scaffolding for central extensions of Teichmüller groupoids, and the page does not reach that application.
transcription_corrections: 'avec op. de μ sur C'' (compatibles avec π de μ sur Ob Φ soit une structure)' should read roughly 'avec op. de μ sur Φ (compatibles avec π, et telles que l'op. de μ sur Ob Φ soit une structure de torseur)'.
'tel que Ob Φ soit E, Soient x,y∈E, torseur sous μ' should read 'tel que Ob Φ soit un torseur sous μ, soit E. Soient x,y ∈ E'. The phrase 'torseur sous μ' belongs before 'soit E'.
In (d), 'examinons, sur 𝒞[?]' is probably 'examinons, sur C' or 'pour y ∈ Ob C', the structure of the fibre categories C'_y.
In (d), the struck word is likely 'groupoïdes associés' (or similar), replaced by 'connexes', giving 'en tant que π-connexes'.
In (b), the struck word before 'f' is unreadable, and the struck tail of the line seems to be 'sur C' (a false start).
